sections_en.text: This document describes the steps of the monthly maintenance of liquid (flooded) batteries. To maintain the batteries in good condition and to continuously verify their fitness for service, a monthly periodic inspection must be carried out to avoid the accumulation of faults on them and thus maintain the required efficiency.

The first draft was prepared by Eng. Saad Mahmoud Mohamed Bassiouny, reviewed by Eng. Adel Abdel Qader El-Nagar of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company, endorsed by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil, General Director of Inspection and Quality Control, and approved by Mr. Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman, Accountant, Head of the Planning and Financial Forecasting Sector and Supervisor of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector.
Issue an approved work order, with the appropriate occupational safety and health category card available to the maintenance team
Smoking is prohibited in the battery room
No flammable materials inside the battery rooms

rows: Suitable tools to verify the soundness of connections
Suitable hydrometer (instrument for measuring acid concentration)
Suitable cleaning tools, suitable cleaning materials
Cleaning tools for floors and batteries
Check the soundness of connections and the tightness of cable terminals, with great care
Use the battery and room floor cleaning tools
Check that the battery room is well ventilated
Check the battery levels against the permitted limit
Measure the concentration of the batteries in which a drop in level was observed
Top up the batteries in which the level dropped, after checking them, with distilled water
Record the monthly observations on the batteries in which the level dropped or which were calibrated.

Introduction
This document describes the steps of the monthly maintenance of liquid (flooded) batteries. To maintain the batteries in good condition and to continuously verify their fitness for service, a monthly periodic inspection must be carried out to avoid the accumulation of faults on them and thus maintain the required efficiency.
The first draft was prepared by Eng. Saad Mahmoud Mohamed Bassiouny, reviewed by Eng. Adel Abdel Qader El-Nagar of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company, endorsed by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil, General Director of Inspection and Quality Control, and approved by Mr. Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman, Accountant, Head of the Planning and Financial Forecasting Sector and Supervisor of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector.
Occupational Safety and Health Precautions
Issue an approved work order, with the appropriate occupational safety and health category card available to the maintenance team
Smoking is prohibited in the battery room
No flammable materials inside the battery rooms
Use the appropriate protective clothing
Issue an approved work order, with the appropriate occupational safety and health category card available to the maintenance team
Smoking is prohibited in the battery room
No flammable materials inside the battery rooms
Use the appropriate protective clothing
Tools, instruments and equipment used
Suitable tools to verify the soundness of connections
Suitable hydrometer (instrument for measuring acid concentration)
Distilled water
Suitable cleaning tools, suitable cleaning materials
Cleaning tools for floors and batteries
Suitable protective clothing
Procedures to be carried out
Check the soundness of connections and the tightness of cable terminals, with great care | 1.
Use the battery and room floor cleaning tools | 2.
Check that the battery room is well ventilated | 3.
Check the battery levels against the permitted limit | 4.
Measure the concentration of the batteries in which a drop in level was observed | 5.
Top up the batteries in which the level dropped, after checking them, with distilled water | 06
Record the monthly observations on the batteries in which the level dropped or which were calibrated. | 07
